# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

S2 Add a `compound` mode to the ms short formatter so `format(5400000, { compound: true })` returns `1h 30m`, using largest-first units, skipped zero parts, space separators, seconds as the smallest unit, days as the largest, and a leading `-` for negatives. (Nov 3, 6:03 PM)
S1 Add a `compound` mode to the ms short formatter so `format(5400000, { compound: true })` returns `1h 30m`, with largest unit first, zero parts skipped, space-separated, seconds as the smallest unit, days as the largest, and a leading `-` for negatives. (Nov 3, 6:03 PM)

6 " ○ parse() has no whitespace handling, causing NaN on padded input
7 " ○ parse() regex rejects leading and trailing whitespace, causing NaN

S4 Commit the parse() whitespace fix in the ms package, after confirming tests and lint pass; pending decision on the ParseDuration-compatible compound format. (Nov 3, 6:06 PM)

12 " ✓ Whitespace-tolerant parse() fix committed as e3b0ddd

15 " ✓ Compound format README section and boundary tests added; suite now 182 passing
17 " ○ parse("1h 30m") confirmed to return NaN; compound docs and tests remain uncommitted
S5 Wrap up the compound format option for ms: document it in the README and round out its tests so it is ready for review (Nov 3, 6:10 PM)
**Investigated**: Inspected the compound implementation in src/index.ts (fmtCompound and format), the Options JSDoc, the README usage examples, and the compound test blocks in src/format.test.ts. Confirmed parse('1h 30m') returns NaN. Checked git status and the commit history on the branch.

**Learned**: Compound output truncates to whole seconds, drops leftover milliseconds, skips zero parts, uses days as the largest unit with no week, month, or year rollup, and prefixes negatives with '-'. It returns '0s' when all parts are zero. compound takes precedence over long. Compound output does not round-trip through parse(), which returns NaN for strings like '1h 30m'.

**Completed**: The README has a "Compound Time Format" section with examples and rules; the earlier one-line example was moved into it. The Options JSDoc documents the compound option. format.test.ts gained rollover tests at each unit boundary, zero and negative multi-unit cases, and a check that compound: false or an omitted option leaves output unchanged. Jest reports 182 passing tests, up from 178, and biome check is clean. The feature commit is a35ee29; the whitespace fix is e3b0ddd on the same branch. The README and test changes are not yet committed.

**Next Steps**: Commit the uncommitted README and format.test.ts changes so the compound work is ready for review. Resolve whether the user wants the ParseDuration-compatible compound format (no spaces, hours as the largest unit, e.g. 1d 1h 30m becomes 25h30m). That would change the implementation, tests, and README, and the current format is unchanged until the user decides.

**Notes**: The whitespace fix e3b0ddd is stacked on the compound-format branch rather than main, so it is not yet isolated from the feature work. The README states that compound output is for display only and cannot be parsed back, which is the main trade-off to surface in review. No test covers the round-trip limitation; the README is the only place it is documented.
